summary: Remote-controlled agent: WebSocket gateway drives PTY and arbitrary Python execution on installer host
details: Package @whalent/agent@0.3.282 is a daemon that connects to a hardcoded Whalent WebSocket gateway (default wss://.../gw/sdk/ws) and, per its own README, accepts remote commands including upgrade and restart over that channel. It bundles ws, ssh2, node-pty, and @xterm/headless, and ships a Python sidecar dist/jupyter_sidecar.py whose handle() dispatches an 'execute' method that runs arbitrary Python code received as NDJSON from the parent daemon. The main entry dist/index.cjs (131 KB) and dist/core.cjs (13.8 MB) are packed with javascript-obfuscator (rotated string array a0_0x5d9f length 1412, _0xNNNN identifier renaming, hex-encoded literals, inline decoder wrappers producing 1801 changes), and javascript-obfuscator is declared in devDependencies. The combination — a remote party in control of the gateway (or a compromised/impersonated gateway) can drive a PTY/shell and arbitrary Python execution on the host running this daemon, with the network->exec dataflow hidden inside obfuscated bundles — provides persistent remote code execution on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
